problem_statement: LangChain's streaming layer is unreliable and inconsistent across model providers and higher-level abstractions (structured output, agents/graphs, tool-calling). Specific failures include: provider-proxied SSE streams that omit the standard 'event:' field (e.g., Anthropic accessed via a Bedrock proxy) causing hard failures with no generation chunks returned; streaming combined with structured output (with_structured_output) producing spurious Pydantic serializer warnings and silently dropping response metadata/headers such as x-request-id; the disable_streaming='tool_calling' flag crashing with an AttributeError because an AsyncStream object is passed where a ChatCompletion is expected, and even when it doesn't crash, disabling streaming globally instead of only for tool-calling turns; and agent/graph execution paths that call ainvoke instead of astream internally, meaning on_llm_new_token callbacks never fire even when graph-level streaming is explicitly enabled. There is also weaker supporting infrastructure: gaps in standard test coverage and release sequencing for tool-call streaming across integration packages, and at least one known-incorrect assertion in the core streaming error-callback test suite that masks whether error-path behavior is actually correct. Collectively these issues mean developers cannot trust that streaming will work uniformly across providers, output modes, and execution paths, forcing workarounds or abandonment of streaming for affected features.
target_user: Developers building LLM applications with LangChain who rely on streaming responses across different providers (including proxied/non-standard endpoints), who use structured output, tool-calling, or agent/graph execution patterns and need consistent token-level streaming and metadata propagation.

acceptance_criteria.given: an Anthropic model is accessed through a Bedrock proxy that sends SSE events without an 'event:' field
acceptance_criteria.then: generation chunks are correctly parsed and returned instead of raising 'No generation chunks were returned'

acceptance_criteria.when: chunks are streamed and the final response is assembled
acceptance_criteria.then: no spurious Pydantic serializer warnings are logged and response metadata including x-request-id is present on the final response

acceptance_criteria.given: disable_streaming='tool_calling' is set on a chat model
acceptance_criteria.then: the turn completes without an AttributeError and without an AsyncStream object being passed where a ChatCompletion is expected

acceptance_criteria.given: disable_streaming='tool_calling' is set on a chat model
acceptance_criteria.then: that turn still streams normally rather than having streaming disabled globally

acceptance_criteria.given: an agent is invoked inside a graph with use_astream=True
acceptance_criteria.then: on_llm_new_token callbacks fire for each token produced, confirming the agent internally used astream rather than ainvoke

acceptance_criteria.given: the core streaming error-callback test suite
acceptance_criteria.when: an error occurs during streaming with no generations produced
acceptance_criteria.then: the test asserts the correct nested-list shape ([[]]) for empty streamed generations, and passes against the corrected implementation

acceptance_criteria.given: an integration package implements tool-call streaming
acceptance_criteria.when: the package's test suite is run against langchain-tests
acceptance_criteria.then: standard tests covering tool-call streaming pass before the stricter langchain-tests version is released

out_of_scope: Adding streaming support for entirely new providers not currently integrated (e.g., full Mistral tool-call streaming support)
Redesigning the overall streaming API/interface (astream, astream_events, callback signatures)
General performance optimization of streaming throughput/latency
Non-streaming structured output correctness issues unrelated to streaming
Building new observability/tracing tooling beyond preserving existing metadata/headers

risks.description: Several of the pain points have frequency of 1, meaning each is backed by a single reported issue; the evidence base for prioritizing these fixes over other work is thin and may not represent the most impactful streaming problems for the broader user base.

Fixing provider-specific SSE parsing (e.g., tolerating missing 'event:' fields) risks masking genuinely malformed responses from other providers or proxies, potentially hiding real errors instead of surfacing them.

Changing disable_streaming='tool_calling' behavior to be turn-scoped rather than global is a behavioral change that could break existing user code relying on the current (buggy) global-disable behavior.
Routing agent/graph execution paths through astream instead of ainvoke may introduce performance or ordering regressions in agent frameworks that were not designed with token-level streaming in mind.

The known-incorrect test assertion (pain point 6) suggests other tests in the streaming suite may also mask incorrect behavior, so fixing only the identified case may leave similar latent issues undetected.
